exports.name: setTimeout
signatures: setTimeout<T extends unknown[]>(callback: (...args: T) => unknown, delay: number, ...args: T): Timeout
exports.description: Schedule execution once after `delay` milliseconds, clamped to a minimum of 1ms.

params.name: callback
params.description: The function to run after the delay.

params.name: delay
params.description: Milliseconds to wait before running; clamped to a minimum of `1`.

exports.name: clearTimeout
signatures: clearTimeout(timer: Timeout): void
exports.description: Cancel a pending timeout, preventing it from firing.

exports.name: setInterval
signatures: setInterval<T extends unknown[]>(callback: (...args: T) => unknown, delay: number, ...args: T): Timeout
exports.description: Schedule repeated execution every `delay` milliseconds, clamped to a minimum of 1ms.

params.name: callback
params.description: The function to run on each interval.

params.name: delay
params.description: Milliseconds between runs; clamped to a minimum of `1`.

exports.name: clearInterval
signatures: clearInterval(timer: Timeout): void
exports.description: Cancel a pending interval, preventing further firings.

exports.description: Cancel a pending immediate, preventing it from firing.

exports.name: Task
exports.description: The base handle shared by `Timeout` and `Immediate`, controlling whether it keeps the event loop alive.

members.name: hasRef
signatures: hasRef(): boolean
members.description: Return whether the task is currently refed, that is keeping the event loop alive.

members.name: ref
signatures: ref(): this
members.description: Ref the task, so it keeps the event loop alive while pending. Returns the task.

members.name: unref
signatures: unref(): this
members.description: Unref the task, so it does not keep the event loop alive while pending. Returns the task.

members.name: refresh
signatures: refresh(): this
members.description: Reset the timeout's delay to start counting from now, rescheduling it without allocating a new handle. Returns the timeout.

exports.description: Schedule execution once after `delay` milliseconds, clamped to a minimum of 1ms.
